status_reasons: THE ROUND-2 DEFECT CLASS IS CLOSED AND I PROVED IT BY DELETING IT. The same untagged six-body fight, killed, crossed over loadState('arena_flat') and killed again with the SAME eids and zero rests, pays 252 then 252 on the shipped tree and 252 then 0 with both guards removed. Round 2 measured this shape as a hard fail. It is not one now.

BUT NEITHER GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING ALONE. Identity ablated by itself: 9/9. Boundary ablated by itself: 9/9. Both: 2/9. The change is not inert, and each half MEASURES inert, which is exactly how the next delete-the-fix on either one comes back green and somebody believes it.

'LEVEL 120 EXACTLY' IS GONE, AND FOR THE RIGHT REASON. Recomputed off game/data/progression/levels.json rather than the piece's own tools: the full clear of 1,124,285 lands at L93 sitting 69.75% into level 94, and all six region cumulatives land between 49% and 73% into their level. Round 1's 2,400,817 landed inside L120. No boundary fitting anywhere.

THE VALUES STAND ON A PLAN, AND THE WORLD'S COPY OF THEM IS 53% STALE. Values are derived at N = 1,230 (RI-WLD07's plan, scale 0.4683); 269 bodies are placed. --census fails closed and says so, which is right. But game/data/world/population-posts.json caches 16,335 souls for the 267 road bodies where the shipped statblocks pay 10,679 — +53.0% on every derived row — and its crossing headline says level 5 where it is level 3. No check in the tree reads both files.

THE 343 ROUTES ARE 14 BEHAVIOURS. 343 exhaustive length-3 routes collapse to 27 distinct paid-signatures and 14 distinct behaviour vectors; 153 of 343 pay zero souls end to end; there are 6 distinct route totals in the entire set; and named_load, save_load and rest have IDENTICAL payment distributions, so the alphabet is nominally 7 events and the oracle can tell 4 apart.

AND THE EXHAUSTIVE ARM FOUND NOTHING. All 12 I3 violations in the INTACT run come from ONE length-5 pattern sampled twice. Zero of the 343 violated anything. The number in the tool's banner contributed no findings.

ONE STATBLOCK, ONE HOUR, 463 ROUTES. Every route drives dres-raid-party (inf_trash at 42) at 12:00; every route total is a multiple of 42. Invariant I2 — 'paid exactly its statblock value x night' — has been tested against one value, and the night half of its own statement is dead in every route the oracle has ever driven.

I1 HAS NEVER BEEN SHOWN ABLE TO FAIL. The builder declared it skipped --self-break. I ran it (59 routes): I2 goes red with 21 violations, I1 stays at 0. Of the two invariants sim/souls.js owns, one still has no demonstrated failure mode.

CONSUMPTION IS REAL AND I PERTURBED ALL FOUR DECLARED VALUES. Statblock souls, the night multiplier, the level curve (funded by killing, not by assignment) and the S15 line all move the world when moved. This is the axis four wave-1 subsystems failed silently and this piece passes it cleanly.

DOCTRINE IS AIRTIGHT AND CHECKABLE. Four writes to soulsHeld in the whole build and exactly one debit — the level. Zero quest files mention souls. Zero hits for gold within 60 characters of a level-up. Bribes are gold. The souls_awarded event carries gold_awarded: 0 on its face.

MY OWN INSTRUMENT WENT RED FOR THE WRONG REASON TWICE AND THE SELF-BREAK GATE CAUGHT BOTH. A level-curve arm that wrote soulsHeld = cost passed under ablation; an attribute arm read getDerivedStats() in a scenario with no character and was reading a 5-key snapshot while claiming 113. Both are declared, both are fixed, and the coverage census is published in the report.

FOUR OF ELEVEN METHODS HAVE NO INSTRUMENT ANYWHERE. The souls tools name methods 1, 2, 6 and 10 only. Method 6 is deliberately never armed. Methods 3, 4, 8 and 11 do not exist in the tree; 5 and 9 are half-covered.

biggest_gap.what: Round 3 re-derived seven enemy statblocks. game/data/world/population-posts.json is GENERATED and caches a souls figure per post plus by_tier, by_region and a crossing summary, all computed against the OLD values, and nothing re-ran it. The world file publishes 16,335 souls for the 267 road bodies where the shipped statblocks pay 10,679 (+53.0%), tier 1 570 against 374, tier 5 5,015 against 3,286, and a crossing headline of 'level_if_fully_cleared: 5' where the true figure today is level 3.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: These are not scratch numbers. W1-POPULATION's round used the crossing figure, and any agent reading the world's placement report gets a soul economy half again too generous. The economy owns the value and the world owns the count, joined by RI-PRG06 §7's normalisation rule — they are one system across two files, and there is no check anywhere in the tree that reads both. This is the same shape as the census amendment the piece exists to honour, one layer out.
biggest_gap.not_a_hard_fail_because: It is a stale generated artifact, not a live defect in the running world. The engine reads the statblocks, not the cached figure, so a player is paid correctly; what is wrong is every number any tool or verdict quotes from that file.

remedy.action: Add a WORLD row to tools/check-souls-corpus.mjs, or a new tools/check-souls-world.mjs: walk game/data/world/population-posts.json, recompute every post's `souls` from game/data/world/encounters.json x the shipped game/data/combat/enemies/*.json, recompute report.souls / report.by_tier / report.by_region / report.crossing.souls / report.crossing.level_if_fully_cleared from those, and fail on any drift. The arithmetic already exists — placedByTier() in tools/progression/derive-soul-values.mjs does exactly this walk against the same three files. Only the comparison against the file's own cached copy is missing. Then W1-POPULATION re-runs tools/world/build-population.mjs so the cached copy is true, and the check is armed AFTER that regeneration, never before (RULES 13).
remedy.acceptance: Three legs, and the middle one is the delete-the-fix. (a) On the tree as it stands today the new check goes RED and names population-posts.json report.souls 16,335 against 10,679 recomputed, plus the five by_tier rows and crossing.level_if_fully_cleared 5 against 3. (b) Change any one statblock's `souls` field by 1 and the check goes RED again, naming that statblock's posts — proving it reads the statblocks and not a second cached copy of its own. (c) Re-run tools/world/build-population.mjs and the check goes GREEN, with `derive-soul-values --census` reporting the same placed-world total as the world file's own report for the first time.

biggest_gap.evidence_note: Recomputed independently in the verdict md §2.1, offline, from game/data/world/population-posts.json x game/data/world/encounters.json x game/data/combat/enemies/*.json: the 267 road bodies at the shipped statblock values sum to 10,679 against the 16,335 the world file caches; the two fog-gate bosses add 3,507 for a placed world of 269 bodies and 14,186 souls, which is exactly what `derive-soul-values --census` reports. The 16,335 in the world file and the 21,664 in the round-2 verdict are two different stale generations of the same number. The arithmetic needs no browser and no artifact of mine to reproduce — it is four files and a sum.

secondary_observations: RI-PRG01 cross-check (method 11's one runnable clause): game/data/progression/levels.json's cost(n) = round(0.015n^3 + 2.00n^2 + 55n + 300) gives cum(120) = 2,391,999, which is RI-PRG06 §1's declared souls_for_L120 exactly. That is the only genuinely falsifiable clause in the corpus-side L120 guard and it holds. The rest of method 11 — the retention figure shared with RI-PRG04 §7 — has no instrument.

--check, the mode that exits 0, prints a -40.6% ANCHOR error against its own stated +/-15% tolerance and a four-row ROSTER GAP without failing. --check --strict fails on exactly those rows and is wired into no project gate. The project's green signal is silent about a 40.6% error. That is RULES 13 followed correctly for the roster gap, but the flag needs a home.

The corpus-side L120 guard is invariant by construction: world_total is §3's own roster sum and souls_for_L120 is §1's own declared figure. The only falsifiable content in it is curve-vs-declared-figure, which is a real cross-item check and passes. The half that would catch a re-tune is in --census and has never fired.

Six of the ten attributes a level can be bought on — agility, speed, intellect, hist-bond, personality, luck — move nothing in the derived sheet or the combat body even at +15. That is RI-PRG02 / W1-21's axis and my snapshot does not cover movement, disposition, loot or skill-use, so it is reported and not charged. It is here because a level is this economy's only sink.

Is a piece scored against methods that have never been buildable, or is the item's method list itself the thing that needs amending? Round 1, round 2 and round 3 have each been marked PROVISIONAL for a version of this and nobody has ruled.

notes: Round 3 is the best round this piece has had and it does not clear the gate. Everything round 2 charged is closed, and I closed the question round 2 could not close — by deleting both guards at once instead of one at a time, and watching six live enemies go back to being worth nothing. What holds it at 6 is that the evidence underneath the good result is thinner than it reads: 343 routes are 14 behaviours over one statblock at noon, the exhaustive arm found nothing, one of the two invariants this file owns has never been shown able to fail, and the values are derived at a census of 1,230 while the world holds 269 and publishes its own copy of those values 53% too high. None of that is a defect a player would meet today. All of it is the difference between a system that is right and a system that has been shown to be right.
